key_insight: Independent foundation models for interatomic potentials share a common, low-dimensional "platonic" geometry in their learned representations, enabling direct cross-model comparison and algebraic operations on embeddings without requiring ground-truth labels.
problem_solved: Different ML interatomic potential models produce incompatible latent representations, hindering model comparison, transfer, diagnostics and ensemble strategies; this work provides a unifying geometric framework to compare and manipulate embeddings across models.
method: Analyze and compare latent embedding spaces from multiple foundation MLIPs to identify a shared low-dimensional geometric structure (the "platonic" geometry).
Develop alignment and embedding-arithmetic procedures to map, add/subtract and compare representations across models.
Demonstrate ground-truth-free diagnostics and cross-model operations that reveal chemically meaningful relationships and enable model-agnostic evaluation.
impact: Enables model-agnostic evaluation, transfer and combination of interatomic potential models, reducing reliance on costly reference calculations and accelerating materials modelling workflows. Practitioners can perform cross-model debugging, interpolation and embeddings arithmetic to build more robust and interoperable ML potentials.
visual_elements: Schematic: multiple clouds (different models) of embeddings aligning onto a single platonic scaffold to show shared geometry.
Vector-arithmetic diagram: example of embedding addition/subtraction mapping to chemical transformations (A + B ≈ C).
Overlay scatter/UMAP: projections of different model embeddings onto the common geometry with color-coded chemical labels to show consistency.
Workflow icon: ground-truth-free diagnostic pipeline vs traditional expensive ab initio validation (cost/time comparison).
paper_title: Platonic representation of foundation machine learning interatomic potentials
